task: Allow timezone selection for cron expression in Scheduler integration creation by threading a timezone parameter through API models, validators, service layers, datasource processors, and the APScheduler CronTrigger engine.

key_reasoning.reason: The timezone parameter must be threaded through CronExpressionValidatorMixin (used in 10+ request models in models/index.py), two validation modules (settings_request_validator.py and scheduler_settings_service.py), two routers (user_settings.py and index.py), two service classes (SchedulerSettingsService and IndexStatusService), BaseDatasourceProcessor._create_or_update_scheduler, and three methods in the Cron trigger engine (__valid_setting, __actualize_cron_job, __create_cron_trigger). The shared mixin red flag bumped this from XL(5) to XXL(6).

Approximately 10 source/infra files modified (models/index.py, settings.py, settings_request_validator.py, scheduler_settings_service.py, index_service.py, user_settings.py router, index.py router, base_datasource_processor.py, cron.py, Dockerfile) plus 5-6 existing test files extended and 1-2 new test files created — total 16-18 files touched, placing this at the XL/XXL boundary; scored XL(5) since most test files are modifications rather than net-new.

Six distinct layers are touched: API request models, API routers, Service business logic (SchedulerSettingsService + IndexStatusService), Datasource Processor layer (BaseDatasourceProcessor), Trigger Engine (Cron), and Infrastructure (Dockerfile tzdata for Alpine). This is a full-stack horizontal threading change.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from XL(5) to XXL(6): CronExpressionValidatorMixin is a core shared utility used in 10+ request models — adding timezone to it constitutes a core shared utility change with wide blast radius
